Nutrition references

These are estimates for specific foods and preparation states. Choose the matching reference product, or compare its label before relying on the estimate. Reference data checked September 9, 2026.

How to measure your ingredients

  • Use the gram weight shown in the recipe when household measures or package sizes differ.
  • Meat weights are cooked edible weights; potatoes and most vegetables are weighed raw. Rice and legumes are measured cooked and drained; pasta and oats are weighed dry. Follow each ingredient's preparation state.
  • Shopping quantities describe the required ingredient state, not an assumed raw purchase weight. Cooking yield varies; use your package yield or weigh after cooking.
  • One US customary cup equals 16 tablespoons or 48 teaspoons. Ounces are weight; fluid ounces are volume. Each food has its own reference weight for household measures. When USDA lists different rounded household weights, PrepFit selects one volume basis consistently.
  • Whey powder is a generic USDA reference, weighed in grams. Supplemental protein means grams of protein, not grams of powder; its other macros and shopping weight are calculated from that same reference. Different brands and scoops vary.
  • Patak's sauce labels report protein as <1 g per 64 g. PrepFit uses zero as a conservative lower bound; actual protein can be up to (but less than) one extra gram per reference serving. Other label values are rounded by their sources.
  • Recipes include only listed ingredients plus water. Additional oils, toppings, or seasonings are outside the estimate and may conflict with your exclusions.

USDA records come from the SR Legacy dataset. Manufacturer panels are linked below. Measurement conventions follow NIST US customary conversions. Values describe reference foods, not laboratory analysis of your prepared meal.

Explicit mixes and sauces

These are PrepFit recipes, not nutrition estimates for unspecified store-bought mixes. Their components appear separately in ingredient and grocery lists. Template portions scale the component recipe; they do not claim a measured final mixture volume.

  • slaw mix: each recipe portion (cup in the template) expands to 56 g cabbage, 22 g carrots.
  • fajita vegetables: each recipe portion (cup in the template) expands to 74.5 g bell peppers, 80 g onion.
  • stir fry vegetables: each recipe portion (cup in the template) expands to 45.5 g broccoli, 27.5 g carrots, 37.25 g bell peppers.
  • tzatziki: each recipe portion (tbsp in the template) expands to 10 g plain Greek yogurt, 4 g cucumber, 0.5 g lemon, 0.25 g garlic, 0.05 g dill.
  • yogurt sauce: each recipe portion (tbsp in the template) expands to 12 g plain Greek yogurt, 2 g lemon, 0.25 g garlic.
  • steak seasoning: each recipe portion (tsp in the template) expands to 0.5 g garlic powder, 0.5 g black pepper, 0.5 g paprika, 0.5 g salt.
  • masala spices: each recipe portion (tsp in the template) expands to 0.6 g cumin, 0.6 g coriander, 0.6 g paprika, 0.2 g black pepper.
